A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed AlgoTrace in v3. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original clustering analyses and primitive-vector intervention experiments, including behavioral effects in Table 2 and compositional induction in Figure 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds harder-TSP clustering, Qwen evaluations, and additional steering controls and statistical analyses.

M1.justification: The clustering, automated annotation, spectral meta-clustering, attention-head averaging, vector injection and composition, and algorithmic fingerprinting procedures are retained. The AlgoTrace name, expanded equations, and evaluations on additional models do not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions cover TSP, 3-SAT, AIME, GraphNav, and synthetic graph-operation and composition tasks. The new 9- and 13-city tracing analyses fall within the TSP complexity range already evaluated in v2 Appendix D, Figure 8. Both GraphNav directions were also already included.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain their unsteered, few-shot, zero-shot, shuffled-context, individual-vector, and composed-vector comparisons. The bag-of-tokens and top-100-token reconstruction controls also remain. Qwen additions concern models on which the intervention comparisons are evaluated, without introducing a competing tracing or steering method.

E3.justification: v3 substantially expands model configurations through Qwen 4B/8B/14B and Base variants, with size-specific attention-head counts. It adds a shared layer-17, magnitude-1.25 evaluation and a parsable-valid-answer metric. The reported expressivity formula is also corrected. Exact Qwen identification is inconsistent: Section 5 says Qwen3.5, while Figure 13 labels Qwen3.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantial validation of primitive tracing on harder TSP instances (Appendix A.8), checks whether final-answer steering produces parsable JSON containing a valid path (Table 10), and tests steering specificity at a common layer and magnitude (Table 13). The earlier bag-of-tokens, reconstruction, and clustering-hyperparameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 newly reports one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests for first/last-node transfer, including significant corresponding interventions and nonsignificant mismatched interventions. Table 14 adds Mann–Whitney U significance reporting for AIME-to-TSP transfer. Existing plotted error bars remain; neither PDF establishes an increase in repeated runs or seeds.

E6.justification: Table 2 and matched earlier control tables retain their numerical values. Substantial new results cover harder-TSP primitive frequencies, Qwen tracing and composition, valid-answer steering, and fixed-setting effects. For example, Table 13 reports a 26.1% reduction in verifications for compare_or_verify2 at the shared setting; this is a new condition, not a correction to Table 2's optimized result.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix A.7, Equation 5 defines expressivity as radius[c]/m[c]; v3 Appendix A.2, Equation 6 changes it to m[c]/radius[c], agreeing with the verbal definition. This is a mathematical correction, while the corresponding expressivity scores and rankings remain unchanged. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The principal tracing, steering, composition, and reasoning-finetuning contributions remain. The abstract's explicit cross-model primitive-transfer assertion in v2 becomes claims about steering multiple model families and transferring across tasks in v3. The conclusion also drops the assertion of identifying universal primitives, modestly narrowing the stated scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds a substantive discussion of primitive granularity, proposing causal inducibility as a criterion and acknowledging that identified primitives may decompose further. It also discusses Euclidean and isotropy assumptions, methodological choice points, and layer-dependent induction. The earlier memorization, task-scope, and nonlinear-composition limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 supplies code and interactive-visualization links where v2 promised future availability. Appendices A.9 and E.2 document Qwen generation settings, an 8096-token limit, and head counts. Most original implementation and hardware details remain. Sampling is still ambiguous because v3's new main-text n=100 statement differs from the retained n=200 in Appendix B.6.

R1.justification: v3 adds Qwen Team (2026), Hu et al. (2026), Nickel and Kiela (2017), and Gu et al. (2019), supporting the added model evaluations, persona-vector comparison, and alternative clustering geometries. The main research positioning is retained; many other reference changes update publication metadata for the same works.

P1.justification: v3 introduces the AlgoTrace name, rewrites the abstract, emphasizes reasoning as a walk through latent space, separates tracing and steering result paragraphs, and moves expressivity earlier in Appendix A. It also revises author information, acknowledgements, and disclosures. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text and references and substantially rearranges the visual presentation. Old Figure 2b and Figure 3c become appendix Figures 6 and 14; Figure 5 gains a task schematic. New harder-TSP and Qwen figures and multiple validation tables expand the displays, alongside revised captions and labels.

improvement.justification: The harder-TSP and Qwen evaluations, valid-answer control, transfer significance tests, corrected expressivity formula, and code-access information strengthen support and reproducibility for the retained framework. These gains are limited by reporting problems: Table 13 shows reduced verification counts despite the accompanying near-general robustness claim, and model naming and extraction sample counts are internally inconsistent. The revision improves scrutiny and documentation without fully resolving the strength of its mechanistic conclusions.
